answer: Coordinated Action Deposit. Each agent action carries a deposit scaled by the count of distinct identities taking the same action in the same window, so parallel clones inflate the deposit for the whole cohort. A grove of agents acting alone pays little; acting in unison raises every member's deposit. Unused deposits return minus a shale-weighted clearing charge. An attacker fielding N clones must lock capital proportional to N squared, making coordination itself the priced scarce good. Identity costs stay ordinary; ivory-level uniqueness is unnecessary.
